statements.t: Note: For the Company’s guidance with respect to fourth quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow, we are not able to provide without unreasonable effort the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, or reconciliation to such GAAP financial measure, because certain items that impact such measures are uncertain, out of the Company’s control or cannot be reasonably predicted.

On the pigment side, operating rates increased sequentially, although we adjusted production levels in response to lower-than-anticipated demand in the quarter, reflecting our continued focus on disciplined cash management.

With two months left in the year, our cost improvement program remains on track to deliver more than $175 million of run-rate savings by the end of 2026, exceeding the high end of our original target.

With the unforeseen prolonged conflict in the Middle East causing both supply chain disruptions and weaker demand in some markets, we now anticipate full year free cash flow to be a use of cash, driven by raw material price headwinds and lower sales volumes resulting in less earnings and lower cash from working capital in the fourth quarter than previously anticipated.
Cost discipline is an ongoing commitment, and as we look ahead, we plan to set cost improvement targets for 2027 and 2028 similar to those of the past two years.
The Company has ample liquidity and does not expect to trigger the springing covenant on the US revolving credit facility.

The Company remains focused on the factors within its control, including reducing anticipated capital expenditures by approximately $30 million for full year 2026, actively managing working capital, and preserving financial flexibility.

risks.t: policy changes affecting international trade, including import/export restrictions and tariffs
continuing inflationary pressures and energy costs, including as it relates to, among other things, natural gas
interest rate and debt market volatility, including in respect of our debt securities
political instability, including the ongoing conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East and any expansion of such conflicts, and other geopolitical events
disruptions in production at our mining and manufacturing facilities
other financial, economic, competitive, environmental, political, legal and regulatory factors

statements.t: In the next twelve months, we expect that our operations will provide sufficient cash for our operating expenses, capital expenditures, interest payments and debt repayments, however, if necessary, we have the ability to borrow under our short-term credit facilities (see Note 13 of notes to the condensed consolidated financial statements).

forecast which could be negatively impacted by items outside of our control, including, among other things, macroeconomic conditions including tariffs, inflationary pressures, political instability including the ongoing Russia and Ukraine and Middle East conflicts and any expansion of such conflicts, and supply chain disruptions.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, our credit rating with Moody’s remained unchanged at B3 negative outlook and our credit rating with Standard & Poor's also remained unchanged at CCC+ positive outlook.

Going forward, we expect to continue to invest in our businesses through cost reduction, as well as growth and vertical integration-related capital expenditures including projects such as our multi-year IT-enabled transformation program , rare earths initiatives and various mine development projects, continued reductions in our debt and continued dividends.
We believe that all of our purchase obligations will be utilized in our normal operations.
